title: I just put $1,000 of real money into my autonomous AI trading system. Here's exactly how I sized it after Reddit tore apart my paper trading results last week.
author: Weird_Night_2176
selftext:
Last week someone in this sub pointed out that without my two best trades (ARM +$2,048 and AMD +$1,741) my system is -$3,232. That comment changed how I went live.

Here's what I changed before flipping the switch:

1. Risk per trade: 2% down to 0.5%. At $1,000 that's $5 max risk per trade. Sized like an experiment, not a validated strategy.

2. Hard kill switch: if the account draws down 10% ($100) the system stops completely. Code-enforced. No overrides.

3. Consecutive loss limit: 5 straight losses and the system pauses. Review required before next entry.

4. P&L tracked two ways: total and with the two outliers stripped. If the stripped line goes negative on live money the AI semiconductor regime has shifted and I shut it down.

The system is a 9/21 EMA crossover with ATR-based stops, RVOL confirming filter, and breakeven lock at +5%. 60 days paper trading. 33% win rate. $999 average winner, $316 average loser.

Markets open Monday at 9:30AM. First real scan fires automatically. I'll post the results next weekend.

Documented the full go-live process here: [https://youtu.be/WbrTX2DkXEY](https://youtu.be/WbrTX2DkXEY)

comments.author: Obviously_not_maayan
comments.body: I think 10% dd is very ambitious, you'll probably find yourself overriding it, in that case why even have that. I would ask about DD in the backtest but I guess you can't really backtest AI agent.
